label: ex:tritium-decay-knot-equation
title: Tritium decay as a Skein crossing change: ${}^3_1\mathrm{H} \to {}^3_2\mathrm{He} + e^- + \nu_e^{\sigma}$
html:
Tritium beta decay written as a knot/link equation.

Tritium \mathcal{N}(1, 2) decays to Helium-3 \mathcal{N}(2, 1). Both have A=3 nucleons consisting of Borromean links joined by Hopf links.

The Skein crossing change. One neutron converts to a proton. This changes the quark content, occurring at a d-d crossing. The knot equation is:

  q  [\mathcal{N}(1, 2)]
  - 
  q^{-1} [\mathcal{N}(2, 1)]
  = 
  (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})
  \left[
    T_{2,3} \sqcup K_{0_1}
  \right]

Markov trace of the transition. The parent and daughter traces differ only at generators \sigma_4 and \sigma_5.

The Q-value in pair Skein units. The Q-value is the sum of pair Skein differences at the 1 internal crossing change and the 6 inter-nucleon crossing changes:

  \mathfrak{Q}_\beta
  = 
  \sum_{k \in \text{modified}} \left(
    \mathcal{S}_{a_k b_k}^{\mathrm{par}}(q)
    - \mathcal{S}_{a_k b_k}^{\mathrm{dau}}(q)
  \right)
  -  m_e

This exact knot equation uses no fitted parameter.
